requirement:
The view of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes` MUST show
each `habeas:coverage` citation attached to the file root or an explicitly
declared function or method. Each entry MUST identify its source item and
source location and show the fenced citation commentary and Rust doc comments
supplying its tracked justification under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor`.
When no tracked justification is present, the entry MUST say so.

File-root citations MUST be labelled as file-threshold exception proposals;
function and method citations MUST be labelled as function exception proposals,
following {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor`.
rationale: structural: No structural obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes.justifications` needs implementation evidence, and the review roots are empty. Every clause describes what the file-notes view shows, so each is observable behavior. - "MUST show each `habeas:coverage` citation attached to the file root or an explicitly declared function or method". This sets which citations appear. A different internal approach, such as a different traversal or data model, would show the same citations, so the choice is discretionary. - "Each entry MUST identify its source item and source location and show the fenced citation commentary and Rust doc comments". This sets the content of the output. It prescribes no named type, field, signature or library. - "When no tracked justification is present, the entry MUST say so". This is an output case, not a structure. - "File-root citations MUST be labelled as file-threshold exception proposals; function and method citations MUST be labelled as function exception proposals". This sets the label text. The reference to `requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor` only supplies the meaning of the exception kinds. That requirement is cited as context and does not prescribe how this view is built. The parent `requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes` requires a file-notes view that identifies the workspace-relative path. That is also observable behavior. No clause prescribes a library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or delegation through a named interface. An alternative implementation could produce the same view in a different way and still satisfy the text. Behavioral tests can cover this requirement, and no {impl} reference is needed for it. behavioral: The tests cover every behavioral obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes.justifications`. **Which citations appear.** `notes_show_root_function_and_method_proposals_with_owned_commentary_and_docs` (`src/execution_coverage/notes.rs`) shows three kinds of entry: - A file-root citation, in the fenced `//!` form. - A function citation. - A method citation, shown as `impl[Worker]/fn[work]`. The same test asserts that a citation on a nested `mod` is not shown as a file exception. It also asserts that the child function's doc comment stays out of the output. `citations_on_modules_and_citation_text_in_literals_do_not_create_explanations` (same file) adds two negative cases. A module citation produces no entry. Citation text inside a string literal produces no entry either. `documentation_includes_non_rust_functions_methods_and_plain_file_roots` (`src/execution_coverage/book.rs`) checks Python, TypeScript and plain-file roots, functions and methods. Their commentary appears in the view. **Source item and location.** The notes test asserts the item label, such as `fn[ordinary]`. It asserts `Source: code.rs:first–last` for each of the four entries. It also asserts `First source citation at line N.` for each. **Justification shown.** The Rust notes test checks that these appear in the view: - Root doc text. - Fenced file-threshold text. - Function and method doc text. - Fenced commentary, with `` escaped. `justification_can_come_from_docs_or_fenced_commentary_but_not_ordinary_comments` covers three separate cases: - Doc comments alone, shown under the `Rust doc comments` heading. - Fenced commentary alone, shown under the `Citation commentary` heading. - An ordinary `//` comment alone, which counts as no justification. In each case it asserts both the presence or absence of the text and the presence or absence of the "No tracked justification" statement. **No justification.** The `fn[unexplained]` entry must say `No tracked justification is present.` The test asserts that exact count of 1. It also asserts the entry has no doc-comment section. **Labels.** The notes test asserts that `File-threshold exception proposal` appears exactly once and `Function exception proposal` exactly three times. The three are the function, the method and the unexplained function. That separates file-root labelling from function and method labelling. The tests do not check the "no justification" statement for a file-root entry. They also do not check the labels on non-Rust items. These are not separate obligations: the requirement does not distinguish them, and the checked cases cover the same required behavior. I did not treat them as gaps.

text: :::{req} index.file_map.notes.justifications
The view of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes` MUST show
each `habeas:coverage` citation attached to the file root or an explicitly
declared function or method. Each entry MUST identify its source item and
source location and show the fenced citation commentary and Rust doc comments
supplying its tracked justification under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor`.
When no tracked justification is present, the entry MUST say so.
File-root citations MUST be labelled as file-threshold exception proposals;
function and method citations MUST be labelled as function exception proposals,
following {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor`.
:::{req} index.file_map.notes
Each listed file provides access to a file-notes view identifying its
workspace-relative path.
:::{req} check.exceptions.anchor
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:coverage` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:
> Cite this on a source file or explicitly declared function to propose a
> coverage exception. Explain in prose why the item's incomplete execution
> coverage is acceptable. Put the explanation in fenced citation commentary
> or Rust doc comments included in the source item's assessed input. An ordinary
> non-doc comment alone does not supply a tracked justification. The reason
> must be substantive; difficulty alone is not a justification.
> On a file's root item, the exception excuses only
> that file's 80% instrumented-line threshold, including absent measurement
> of its executable code. On an explicit function with a body, it excuses
> that function's recorded zero execution or absence from otherwise usable
> measurement, without excusing the file's threshold.
> The explanation must agree with the current source and any callers or
> configuration assumptions on which it relies. Only a current accepted
> independent assessment permits the exception. A file exception does not
> excuse unexecuted or not-measured functions in that file.
> The citation applies to its source item without conditional build matching
> and may remain when measured coverage satisfies the item's obligations.
Only `{cite}` MAY reference this built-in, inline or fenced using the standard
reference forms of {cite}`requirements.references.roles`. The built-in MUST be
available in every project without a project requirement, site query, or
exception-specific configuration.
